definition: Semaphore means a system of visual signals.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word semaphore. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know semaphore should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Before the airfield bought radios, a man on the roof worked semaphore, spelling wind warnings to pilots two fields away.
A gesture is the loose end of the line — one motion, meaning roughly whatever the crowd decides — while semaphore fixes every meaning in advance, an agreed alphabet with nothing left to guess.
A signal stops short of semaphore — one agreed sign with one agreed meaning, where semaphore is a whole alphabet that can spell anything you can say.

Flag code is the schoolyard name for the same two-flag alphabet, and in casual talk the two overlap almost completely. Semaphore is the proper term — the one a navy manual or a railway rulebook uses — and it also covers arm positions and railway blades, not flags alone.

Signaling is the whole craft of sending messages by agreed signs — lamps, flags, smoke, whistles together. Semaphore is one codified system inside that craft: a fixed visual alphabet of positions that can spell anything. All semaphore is signaling; most signaling is not semaphore.

The two lighthouse families lived a mile of open water apart, and their children did homework together anyway — by semaphore.
Each porch kept a pair of red-and-yellow flags, and each child had memorized the alphabet of positions: arms at four and eight o'clock for one letter, straight out for another.
Math answers took forever.
But the system never failed in any fog thin enough to see through, because nothing about it was guesswork — every pose meant one letter, agreed years before either child was born.
When the older girl finally visited the mainland school, she found note-passing primitive: fold, toss, hope.
Her code crossed a mile of sea.
